'''Paul Jerome Hall''' (born February 21, 2002) is an American [[basketball]] player for the [[Charlotte Hornets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Greensboro Swarm]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson Tigers]].

==Early life and high school career==
Hall, a [[Center (basketball)|center]] from [[Spartanburg, South Carolina]], committed to Clemson out of [[Dorman High School]] as the top recruit in South Carolina and state player of the year.<ref>{{cite web|first=Scott|last=Keepfer|title=PJ Hall, SC's No. 1-ranked basketball prospect, commits to Clemson|url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/2019/10/23/clemson-basketball-gets-commitment-states-top-rated-player/4074056002/|website=GreenvilleOnline.com|publisher=[[The Greenville News]]|date=October 23, 2019|access-date=December 9, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:PJ Hall and Hayden Brown (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Hall against Hayden Brown in 2022|256x256px]]
Hall was a reserve as a freshman, then entered the starting lineup his [[sophomore]] season, raising his scoring average from 3.5 to 15.5 points per game.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jon|last=Blau|title=Clemson basketball star PJ Hall discovers purpose in trying seasons|url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/clemson/clemson-basketball-pj-hall-overcomes-adversity/article_240f277e-83d6-11ee-831d-db98cab37a30.html|website=PostAndCourier.com|publisher=[[The Post and Courier]]|date=November 16, 2023|access-date=December 9, 2023}}</ref> As a junior, he averaged 15.3 points and 5.7 rebounds and was named third-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hunter Tyson named all-ACC first team; PJ Hall earns third team honors|url=https://clemsontigers.com/tyson-hall-all-acc/|website=ClemsonTigers.com|publisher=[[Clemson Tigers]]|date=March 6, 2023|access-date=December 9, 2023}}</ref> Following the season, Hall declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]], but maintained his eligibility to keep the option of returning to college. Ultimately he chose to return to Clemson, despite earning an invitation to the [[NBA draft combine]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Isaac|last=Trotter|title=Why Clemson star PJ Hall exited the NBA Draft, denied the transfer portal and returned for his senior season|url=https://247sports.com/article/pj-hall-clemson-nba-draft-joe-girard-iii-transfer-portal-brad-brownell-ncaa-tournament-210731720/|website=247sports.com|publisher=[[247Sports]]|date=May 25, 2023|access-date=December 9, 2023}}</ref>

To start the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]], Hall was named to the preseason All-ACC team and included in the [[John R. Wooden Award|Wooden Award]] and [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar Award]] watch lists. On December 5, he was named the ACC Player of the Week after averaging 21.5 points and 9.5 rebounds in wins over [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] and [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]].<ref>{{cite web|title=PJ Hall earns ACC player of the week honor|url=https://clemsontigers.com/pj-hall-earns-acc-player-of-the-week-honor/|website=ClemsonTigers.com|publisher=[[Clemson Tigers]]|date=December 4, 2023|access-date=December 9, 2023}}</ref> Hall averaged 18.3 points, 6.4 rebounds, 1.4 assists, and 1.4 blocks per game.<ref>{{cite news|first=Evan|last=Massey|title=Clemson Basketball Star PJ Hall Receives Intriguing Comparison Before NBA Draft|url=https://www.si.com/college/clemson/men-s-basketball/clemson-basketball-star-pj-hall-receives-intriguing-comparison-before-nba-draft-evan9|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=June 21, 2024|access-date=July 1, 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Denver Nuggets / Grand Rapids Gold (2024–2025)===
After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Hall joined the [[Denver Nuggets]] for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]]<ref>{{cite web|title=DENVER NUGGETS ANNOUNCE 2024 NBA SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER AND MINI-CAMP SCHEDULE|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-announce-2024-nba-summer-league-roster-and-mini-camp-schedule|website=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2024|access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref> and on July 10, 2024, he signed a two-way contract with the team.<ref>{{cite web|title=NUGGETS SIGN HALL AND ALEXANDER TO TWO-WAY CONTRACTS|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-hall-and-alexander-to-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2024|access-date=July 19, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Marc|last=Whiteman|title=Clemson's PJ Hall agrees to terms with Denver Nuggets|url=https://www.wyff4.com/article/clemsons-pj-hall-hopes-to-hear-name-called-on-day-2-of-nba-draft/61431607|website=WYFF4.com|date=June 27, 2024|access-date=July 1, 2024}}</ref> He made 19 appearances for Denver during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 1.7 points, 1.2 rebounds, and 0.2 assists.

===Memphis Grizzlies / Hustle (2025)===
On July 21, 2025, Hall signed a two-way contract with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 20, 2025 |title=Grizzlies' PJ Hall: Signs two-way deal with Memphis |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-pj-hall-signs-two-way-deal-with-memphis/ |access-date=July 21, 2025 |website=CBSSports.com |language=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Grizzlies sign PJ Hall to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-pj-hall-to-two-way-contract|access-date=December 4, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}}</ref> He appeared in seven games for the Grizzlies, averaging 1.9 points, 1.3 rebounds, and 0.3 assists. Hall was waived by Memphis following the signing of [[Jahmai Mashack]] on November 16.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Grizzlies Sign Jahmai Mashack to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-jahmai-mashack-to-two-way-contract|access-date=November 30, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Charlotte Hornets / Greensboro Swarm (2025–present)===
On December 24, 2025, Hall signed a two-way contract with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=December 24, 2025|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign PJ Hall|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-sign-pj-hall|access-date=December 24, 2025|website=nba.com}}</ref> He made 12 appearances (including two starts) for the Hornets during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 6.1 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 0.7 assists (all career-highs). On April 9, 2026, Hall was ruled out for the remainder of the season after undergoing surgery to repair a right ankle fracture he had suffered playing for the [[Greensboro Swarm]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hornets' PJ Hall: Won’t return in 2025-26|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/hornets-pj-hall-wont-return-in-2025-26/|access-date=April 24, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref>
